IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`
- Hermes Agent: `references/hermes-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>"

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which

those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/status-report

# Status Report

Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report — an email to **Kenny Boyd and
Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly ("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), every two weeks, ~270 words.

Governed by **KR 4.1** in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3). Read that KR as a
**content checklist** — shipped work, work in flight, decisions needed, anything at risk,
what's next — not as a layout. Eric's real reports run as flat prose with no section
headers. See **Voice** below; match it.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
for; do not let it slip out of the output.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` for all paths — never hardcode. Keys used
here: `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`,
`vault_status_reports`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_scoreboard`,
`okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`.

Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
Output dir: `{vault_status_reports}`

> The config held Windows paths from the pre-migration machine until 2026-08-11. If any
> value starts with `C:\`, stop and fix the config first — every skill that trusts it is
> broken until you do.

## Relationship to other skills

- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.

---

## Step 1 — Establish the period

Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.

**Count sends.** KR 4.1's target is "≥3 **sent** by Aug 31," and writing a file is not
sending it. Count files in `{vault_status_reports}` with `sent: true` in frontmatter —
that is the real number. Report progress toward ≥3 in Step 8. If files exist with
`sent: false` older than a week, ask whether they actually went out; an uncounted send
is as bad for the KR as a missed one.

A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.

**Cadence is settled: every two weeks.** Eric committed to it in writing in the first
report — "Starting these updates every two weeks." Report 1 went out **2026-08-24**, so
sends land on even fortnights from there (2026-09-07, 09-21, 10-05, …). The earlier
"twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday" plan was an assistant assumption and is retired.

## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)

### Step 2a — Preflight the meeting source

Run `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5` first.

**Fixed 2026-08-11** — the key is in `~/.zshrc` and the local mirror was rebuilt with
`fireflies-pp-cli sync`; as of 2026-08-13 the key is visible to the Bash tool directly.
The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`, not `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/`.

If it fails again, `unable to open database file: out of memory (14)` means the mirror is
**missing, not corrupt** — run `sync` before anything else. Then:

- **Do not hard-stop.** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure; this skill must not,
  or it inherits the outage that already lapsed `weekly-review`.
- **Fall back** to reading `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` filtered to the period by the
  `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename prefix. These files have **no YAML frontmatter** — parse the
  prepended header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) and the
  Fireflies export sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
- **Check staleness and say so.** Compare the newest meeting file's date to today. If
  the gap is >2 days, tell the user plainly in Step 8: *"Meeting data is stale through
  {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."* A silently incomplete
  report is worse than a flagged one — the user is about to send it to a supervisor.
- Record the degraded source in the internal record's frontmatter.

### Step 2b — Pull

Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.

1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
   (flags verified valid; `--since` accepts `7d`/`24h` form). Gives titles, gists,
   topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}`.
   On failure, use the 2a fallback.
2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
   (`--from` takes an integer number of days). Flag anything open >14 days; those are
   risk-section candidates. On failure, parse `## Action items` blocks from the vault
   meeting files instead.
3. **Shipped artifacts** — read `{vault_output_ledger}`, newest first, entries within
   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**

   Format is a markdown table, newest first, data rows starting at line 22:
   `| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |` where *Shipped* is `YYYY-MM-DD`,
   *Artifact* is the short name, *What it is* is a dense paragraph, and *Harvest* holds
   `[[wikilinks]]` or is empty. Match rows with `^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by
   date. Compress *What it is* to one clause for the email — those paragraphs run long
   and will blow the 300-word ceiling if pasted whole.
4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs). This is the **only** trustworthy KR
   source. Two others will lie to you:

   - **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — superseded v2 set of 9.
   - **Do not trust `{okr_scoreboard}` for confidence values.** It was generated
     2026-06-12 against the retired *quarterly, 3-objective* set and scores KRs that no
     longer exist; v3's fourth objective (Leadership & Visibility) isn't in it at all.
     Its `Conf` decimals are real numbers attached to dead targets. If it still predates
     the v3 restructure (2026-07-17), tell the user it needs regenerating — `okrs.yaml`
     is the source of truth, `okr.py` regenerates `SCOREBOARD.md` and `okrs.json` — and
     report KR status from `{okr_doc}` alone in the meantime.

6. **Sport roster** — the 17-program list for the coverage panel comes from
   `{utilization_brief}` §"Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the two XC / Track &
   Field rows each bundle two programs). Never re-derive this list from memory. Note it
   is *prescriptive* — what each program could use — not a record of current activity,
   which is exactly why the coverage panel is worth publishing.
7. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
8. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.

### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage

`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
stage feeds *In Progress*.

## Voice — match the real thing, not the spec

**Read `{vault_status_reports}/2026-08-24-email-sent.txt` before drafting.** That is the
first report Eric actually sent. It is the reference for how he writes; this skill's
earlier draft was never sent and should not be imitated.

What his email actually does:

- **No section headers.** Flat short paragraphs, one topic each, no Shipped / In Progress
  / Decisions Needed labels. Do not impose the KR 4.1 headers on his prose — they are the
  *content checklist*, not the layout. Make sure each of the five things is covered
  somewhere; do not label them.
- **One framing line up top**, then straight into it. No preamble.
- **"We" for department work, "I" for his own actions.** He writes as the unit.
- **Concrete and operational.** Equipment, buildings, people, dates: Perch cameras at
  Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar, survey cutoff August 28th. Names people
  freely — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi, Micah.
- **Asks come last and land soft:** "One ask I wanted to run past you both is whether…"
  Do **not** convert these into "need Chris by Aug 31." That register is more forceful
  than he writes and it will read as someone else's words.
- **Stalled things get passed along, not escalated:** "still haven't heard back. Passing
  that along in case a nudge is warranted."
- **About 270 words. No attachment.** The memo PDF exists for when something needs to be
  handed across a table; the ordinary cycle is email only.

### The sourcing gap this exposed — important

Almost nothing in his real report appears in `portfolio.json` or `_ledger.md`: survey
response rates, camera installs at three buildings, heart-rate monitors arriving for
tennis, staff meeting cadence, a stalled email to Micah. Those sources track his
**building** work. He reports his **departmental operations**.

So the auto-pull covers maybe a third of what belongs in the report. **Weight the
interview accordingly** — ask about equipment, deliveries, installs, staffing, meetings
held, and follow-ups awaiting a reply, not just what moved in the registry. Treat a draft
built only from automated sources as roughly one-third finished.

## Step 3 — Draft before asking

Write a complete draft of all five sections from the pull. Cut to **5–6 projects with
real motion** — never a 14-line roster. Projects that didn't move go to the internal
record and, if relevant, the sport coverage panel.

Tag every Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*,
*(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*.

Then identify the gaps — that is what the interview is for.

## Step 4 — Interview the gaps only

Ask in **one batch**, not serially. Keep it to what the pull genuinely couldn't answer.
Lead with targeted gap questions, then the four standing ones.

**Targeted** (generated from the pull, examples):
- "Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything from them that Chris needs?"
- "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period — is that right, or did something go out
  that never got logged?"
- "Kinexon_Volleyball hasn't moved in the registry since July. Stalled, or just not
  logged?"

**Standing** (every time). The first three carry most of the report — they cover the
operational half no automated source sees:

1. **Equipment, installs, deliveries.** What arrived, what got installed where, what's
   being phased out, who's onboarding onto it. Eric's real reports lead with this
   (Perch cameras at Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar for tennis).
2. **Meetings held and staffing.** Who he met with, what came out of it, changes to
   cadence or who attends. Names matter — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi.
3. **Conversations no transcript caught** — hallway, text, sideline, phone. Invisible to
   every automated source, and among the highest-value things this interview captures.
4. **Anything waiting on someone else.** Unanswered emails, pending approvals, stalled
   follow-ups. These become the soft "passing that along" lines at the end.
5. **Anything about to go sideways** that Chris and Kenny should hear from him first.
   *(Push here. An always-empty risk line means it isn't being used honestly.)*
6. **Any ask** — time at a meeting, a decision, a nudge. Phrased softly, at the end.
7. **Ideas generated** — worth parking, pitching, or building?
8. **What's next** for the coming two weeks.

Also ask, if the pull shows thin coverage: *"Any sport you touched this period that
isn't showing up in my sources?"* Non-revenue involvement is the whole point and it is
the most likely thing to be undercounted.

## Step 5 — Assemble and check

Fill the template at `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`.

Run every check before showing the user anything:

- [ ] **Email body is under 300 words.** Count it. State the count. Over the ceiling,
      cut — do not negotiate with yourself.
- [ ] **Every Shipped line traces to a `_ledger.md` entry.** No exceptions.
- [ ] **No endorsement claimed that doesn't exist.** If sign-off is pending, "our
      standard intake process," never "the approved process."
- [ ] **Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag.**
- [ ] **Every Decisions Needed item names a person and a date.** No owner or no date
      means it isn't a decision request — rewrite or cut it.
- [ ] **Jargon table enforced.** No CMJ, ACWR, asymmetry index, unexplained B.A.I.R.
- [ ] **Never "one unified dashboard."** The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke
      on top."
- [ ] **Research presented as research** — no readiness or deployment claims.
- [ ] **Risks section is non-empty** unless the user explicitly confirmed there's
      nothing. Ask once more before letting it go empty.
- [ ] **Repeat check:** any Decisions Needed item carried over from the previous report
      gets flagged to the user — two unanswered asks means the email has failed at it
      and it needs raising in person.
- [ ] **Email and PDF agree.** The two are filled separately, so verify it: every
      Shipped, In Progress, Decisions Needed, and Risks item in the email appears in the
      PDF. The PDF may carry *more* detail — it must never carry different facts, a
      different sport tag, or a different date. Sending a supervisor two versions of the
      same report is the failure this check exists to prevent.
- [ ] **Sport coverage panel is not padded.** Untouched sports stay marked untouched. A
      thin panel is real information; a padded one destroys the evidentiary value of
      every honest panel before and after it.

## Step 6 — Emit

Produce three things:

1. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record, full Layer 3
   structure from the template: email as sent, meetings held, conversations, ideas, full
   roster, KR ledger, and the "Not for the report" candid section.
2. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — render
   `assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content. One page, always.

   **It is a printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Single column, one serif family,
   letterspaced small-cap section heads, one green hairline. Never reintroduce status
   dots, badge or pill rows, bolded stat lines, progress bars, or a two-column grid —
   that vocabulary is what made the first version read as generated.

   **Measure before shipping**, don't eyeball it. Budget is **950px of content at 666px
   width**:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "s=open('<file>.html').read(); open('/tmp/probe.html','w').write(
     s.replace('</body>','<script>window.addEventListener(\"load\",()=>{document.title=
     \"H:\"+Math.round(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)})</script></body>'))"
   "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless --disable-gpu \
     --virtual-time-budget=3000 --window-size=666,1200 --dump-dom file:///tmp/probe.html \
     | grep -o '<title>H:[0-9]*'
   ```

   Then render: `--headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=<out>`.
   Over 950px, **cut prose** — never drop below 9.6pt. This gets printed and read by
   people who will not squint for you.
3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.

### Do not send

The connected Gmail account is the user's **personal** address
(`eric.rash11@gmail.com`), not Baylor. Do not create Gmail drafts — they would land in
the wrong mailbox. The user sends from Outlook on the work account.

Never send a report to a supervisor without the user reading it first, under any
circumstance.

## Step 7 — Log

- Append shipped artifacts to `{vault_output_ledger}` if the interview surfaced any that
  weren't logged.
- Update `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` with confirmed status, sport, and KR
  mapping — this keeps the canonical spine current as a byproduct rather than a chore.
- Add an `updates[]` entry to `{portfolio_json}` for each project reported as moved, via
  the `project` skill, so the registry stops being empty.
- Set `sent: false` in the internal record. The user flips it after sending.

## Step 8 — Report to the user

State: word count, report number, next send date, which sports appeared, anything the
checks flagged, and where the three files landed.

---

## Failure modes to design against

**Padding.** A thin period is a legitimate output. "Nothing shipped this period" is an
honest line that protects the word "shipped" everywhere else. Inflating a quiet period
is the fastest way to make the report worthless — and to make the time documentation
inadmissible when it matters.

**Roster creep.** The email is not a project list. 14 status lines reads as 14 things
half-done. Five moving projects reads as focus.

**The credit goal quietly disappearing.** The report exists so non-football,
non-basketball involvement becomes visible. If a period's coverage panel is thin, that
is real information and it should be shown, not hidden — a padded panel destroys the
evidentiary value of every honest one.

**Depending on another ritual.** `weekly-review` lapsed for seven weeks earlier this
year. This report must never require it.
Let me look at the config and the last report.

# Output Ledger — Shipped Artifacts

Running record of things that actually shipped: deliverables handed off, talks
given, pipelines gone live, decisions locked. One line each, newest first.
Maintained by the `/harvest` skill (every harvest appends here) and by hand.

This is also the career-facing proof-of-work record — the answer to "what have
you shipped?" should be readable straight off this page.

---
name: interview-me
description: End-of-workday structured interview that distills the user's day into atomic permanent notes for their SecondBrain Obsidian vault. NOT a journaling app — produces curated synthesis notes, not stream-of-consciousness. Use when the user types `/interview-me`, says "interview me", "let's debrief", "end of day interview", "process my day", "wrap up today", or otherwise asks to capture their workday for their second brain.
---

# Interview Me

End-of-workday synthesis ritual. The user is a sport-science / performance analyst who writes essays connecting sport science, product strategy, and decision-making. The interview's job is to extract publishable insights, not to record what happened.

## Vault location

`/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain/`

**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.

- `Inbox/` — full transcripts (one per day)
- `Notes/` — atomic permanent notes (one idea per file)
- `Drafts/` — essays in progress
- `Archive/` — published
- `Templates/interview-note.md`, `Templates/permanent-note.md`

## The interview

**Time budget:** 10–15 minutes. If the user wants to keep talking, schedule a follow-up session — don't blow the budget.

**Opening line (verbatim is fine):**
> Let's debrief. Four short questions, then I write up anything that earned its place. Ready?

### Question 1 — Orientation (filter)
> What did you spend time on today?

Listen for themes. Don't try to capture everything. Look for: a hard decision, a piece of work that consumed a lot of time, anything that felt different from yesterday.

### Question 2 — Signal (insight detection)
> What surprised you, frustrated you, or changed your mind?

This is the gold question. Genuine surprise, frustration, or updated belief = the moments worth writing down. If the answer is "nothing," probe once: *"Nothing at all? Even small recalibrations count."* If still nothing, accept and move on — not every day produces signal.

### Question 3 — Pattern (synthesis)
> Does anything from today connect to what you were thinking about earlier this week or recently?

**Optional aid:** quietly Glob `Notes/*.md` modified in the last 7 days; if you find 2–3 candidates that match today's themes, name them and ask if today's experience updates them.

### Question 4 — Essay seed (publishable insight)
> If you told a peer one thing about today's work, what would it be?

This question converts experience into transferable insight. If the user gives a great one-liner — capture it verbatim as the seed for a permanent note.

## Optional source pull-ins

Offer when the user references them. Don't pull unprompted.

- **Meeting referenced** ("today's call with X", "this morning's standup"):
  → **First, check `Inbox/meetings/` for a local summary** — Glob for files matching the date or participant. If found, read and quote from the local file (free, fast, no API call).
  → If not found locally, ask: *"Want me to pull from Fireflies?"* → invoke the `meeting-sync` skill to sync the latest meetings, then read the local file.
  → Fall back to direct `pp-fireflies` only if `meeting-sync` reports nothing matching.
- **Paper / article referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the source from Zotero?" → use `pp-zotero-research-library` skill.
- **GPS / Catapult data referenced:**

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/CreateSkill

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/CreateSkill/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


## 🚨 MANDATORY: Voice Notification (REQUIRED BEFORE ANY ACTION)

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the CreateSkill skill to ACTION"}' \
     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **CreateSkill** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# CreateSkill

Complete skill development lifecycle: **structure** (create, validate, canonicalize) + **effectiveness** (test, improve, optimize triggers). Structural workflows ensure skills follow LifeOS conventions. Effectiveness workflows — inspired by Anthropic's skill-creator — ensure skills actually work and trigger reliably.

## Enforcement

Handrolling skill files — writing `SKILL.md` or `Workflows/`, `Tools/`, `References/` by hand — is forbidden by `skills/CLAUDE.md`. Spawn this skill first and let it orchestrate. Reading these workflows and performing the steps yourself is the exact anti-pattern the rule exists to prevent.

This skill is the **single home** for skill authoring here. `write-a-skill` is a pointer to it; `superpowers:writing-skills` is a third-party plugin skill and is not the authority in this workspace. (Consolidated 2026-08-15.)

*This text used to live in the frontmatter `description`. Descriptions load into every session's system prompt, so enforcement prose belongs in the body — the description now carries only what is needed to trigger.*

## Authoritative Source

**Before creating ANY skill, READ:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md`

**Canonical example to follow:** any well-formed public skill in `~/.claude/skills/` (e.g. `Research/SKILL.md`, `Daemon/SKILL.md`, `CreateSkill/SKILL.md` itself).

## Naming Convention — Public vs Private

**Skill name encodes its public/private status. There are exactly two valid forms.**

| Skill type | Directory format | Example | Allowed content |
|------------|------------------|---------|-----------------|
| **Public** | `TitleCase` | `Blogging`, `Daemon`, `CreateSkill` | Templated, safe, generic, ready for public release |
| **Private** | `_ALLCAPS` (underscore prefix, all uppercase) | `<your-release-skill>`, `_INBOX`, `_BROADCAST`, `_DOTFILES` | Anything personal, sensitive, identity-bound, customer-bound, or environment-specific |

**The leading underscore is the public-release boundary.** Release tooling skips `_*` skills entirely — they never leave `~/.claude`. Public skills (no underscore) are mirrored into the LifeOS public release and MUST contain only generic, templated content.

**Sub-file naming (both public and private skills):**

| Component | Format | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Workflow files | `TitleCase.md` | `Create.md`, `UpdateDaemonInfo.md` |
| Reference docs | `TitleCase.md` | `ProsodyGuide.md`, `ApiReference.md` |
| Tool files | `TitleCase.ts` | `ManageServer.ts` |
| Help files | `TitleCase.help.md` | `ManageServer.help.md` |

**Wrong (NEVER use):**
- Skill dirs: `createskill`, `create-skill`, `CREATE_SKILL` (no underscore + caps for public; no kebab/snake for private)
- Files: `create.md`, `update-info.md`, `SYNC_REPO.md`

### Choosing public vs private — the decision rule

Ask: **"Could this skill be dropped, as-is, into a stranger's `~/.claude/skills/` and just work?"**

- **Yes** → public skill (`TitleCase`). Body must be generic; user-specific config layers in via `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/<SkillName>/`.
- **No, because it references my identity, my contacts, my business, my customer, my paid API, my private infra, my domain, my private repo, my partner, or my financial/health/security data** → private skill (`_ALLCAPS`).

**When in doubt, build it private first (`_ALLCAPS`). Promoting `_FOO` → `Foo` later is easy. Discovering a public skill leaks your life is permanent.**

---

## Public Release Readiness (MANDATORY)

**Public skills (`TitleCase`) ship to the world. Private skills (`_ALLCAPS`) never leave the local repo.** Sensitivity is decided by skill name, not by per-file scrubbing at share-time.

### The Bright Line

**Public skill (`TitleCase`) — content rule:**

ONLY templated, safe, public, ready content. Period.

- ✅ Generic instructions any LifeOS user could follow
- ✅ Templated patterns with placeholders for user-specific values
- ✅ Public API references and dependencies on public tools
- ❌ Real names (people, products, companies, customers)
- ❌ Real domains, hostnames, IPs, internal URLs
- ❌ API keys, tokens, credentials, session cookies, OAuth secrets — even example-looking ones
- ❌ Private repo paths or references (`github.com/<org>/<private-repo>`)
- ❌ Customer data, customer-specific workflows, customer engagement context
- ❌ First-person war stories tied to a specific incident, project, or person
- ❌ User-specific filesystem paths (`/Users/<name>/...`, `/home/<name>/...`)
- ❌ Identity-bound preferences (DA name, principal name, partner name, pet name, financial figures, health data)

**Private skill (`_ALLCAPS`) — content rule:**

Anything goes. Real names, real domains, real customers, real credentials-by-reference (env var names, never values), real war stories, real internal infra. The underscore IS the safety boundary. These skills are excluded from release tooling.

### The Decision Test

When you find yourself wanting to write any of the following into a skill body, that skill MUST be `_ALLCAPS`:

| If the skill mentions… | Skill must be |
|------------------------|---------------|
| A specific person's name (yours, your partner's, your team's, a customer's) | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific product name you own or sell | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific customer or client | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific paid API account, billing realm, or subscription | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific private domain, hostname, internal IP, or VPN | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific private repo, dotfile location, or local infra | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific business process tied to your company | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific financial, health, security, or legal context | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific incident or one-off war story | `_ALLCAPS` |
| Anything that would be wrong, embarrassing, or unsafe in someone else's `~/.claude/` | `_ALLCAPS` |

If none of the above apply and the skill is fully generic — it can be `TitleCase` (public).

### Where Personal Layering Goes for Public Skills

A public skill can be made user-specific at runtime via `~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/<SkillName>/PREFERENCES.md`. The skill body stays generic; the user's customization file overlays per-instance context. Use this when a skill is fundamentally generic but benefits from per-user tweaks (preferred voice, default formats, personal taste).

**Do not use SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS to smuggle private content into a public skill.** If the skill *requires* private context to function (real customer name, real API account, real internal infra), it is a private skill — name it `_ALLCAPS` and stop.

### Allowed in Public Skills

- Generic `~/` paths (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/Projects/<tool>/`) — resolve per-user
- Public repo URLs for tools the skill depends on
- Public API endpoints that are conventions, not secrets (e.g., `localhost:31337/notify`)
- Example values clearly marked as placeholders (`<url>`, `<SESSION_ID>`, `test@example.com`)
- Generic env var *names* (never values): `STRIPE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`

### Pre-Flight Grep (Public Skills Only)

Before shipping or modifying any `TitleCase` skill, run:
```bash
rg -i "<your-name>|<your-org>|<your-product>|<your-domain>|/Users/[a-z]+/" ~/.claude/skills/<SkillName>/
```

Zero matches = ready for public release. Any match = either scrub it, move it to SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS, or rename the skill to `_ALLCAPS` and stop pretending it's public. **`_ALLCAPS` skills are exempt from this grep — they are private by design.**

---

## Flat Folder Structure (MANDATORY)

**CRITICAL: Keep folder structure FLAT - maximum 2 levels deep.**

### The Rule

**Maximum depth:** `skills/SkillName/Category/`

### ✅ ALLOWED (2 levels max)

```
skills/SkillName/SKILL.md                    # Skill root
skills/SkillName/Workflows/Create.md         # Workflow - one level deep - GOOD
skills/SkillName/Tools/Manage.ts             # Tool - one level deep - GOOD
skills/SkillName/QuickStartGuide.md          # Context file - in root - GOOD
skills/SkillName/Examples.md                 # Context file - in root - GOOD
```

### ❌ FORBIDDEN (Too deep OR wrong location)

```
skills/SkillName/Resources/Guide.md              # Context files go in root, NOT Resources/
skills/SkillName/Docs/Examples.md                # Context files go in root, NOT Docs/
skills/SkillName/Workflows/Category/File.md      # THREE levels - NO
skills/SkillName/Templates/Primitives/File.md    # THREE levels - NO
skills/SkillName/Tools/Utils/Helper.ts           # THREE levels - NO
```

### Allowed Subdirectories

**These subdirectories are allowed:**
- **Workflows/** - Execution workflows ONLY
- **Tools/** - Executable scripts/tools ONLY
- **References/** - Extended reference material for large skills (API docs, detailed guides)

**Context files (documentation, guides, references) go in the skill ROOT or in References/.**

**When to use References/:** When SKILL.md exceeds ~500 lines and has substantial reference content (API signatures, detailed examples, troubleshooting guides). Keep SKILL.md as a routing guide; move encyclopedic content to References/.

### Why

1. **Discoverability** - Easy to find files
2. **Simplicity** - Less navigation overhead
3. **Speed** - Faster file operations
4. **Consistency** - Every skill follows same pattern

**If you need to organize many workflows, use clear filenames instead of subdirectories:**

**See:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md` (Flat Folder Structure section)

---

## Dynamic Loading Pattern (Large Skills)

**For skills with SKILL.md > 100 lines:** Use dynamic loading to reduce context on skill invocation.

### How Loading Works

**Session startup:** Only frontmatter loads for routing
**Skill invocation:** Full SKILL.md loads
**Context files:** Load only when workflows reference them

### The Pattern

**SKILL.md** = Minimal (30-50 lines) - loads on skill invocation
- YAML frontmatter with triggers
- Brief description
- Workflow routing table
- Quick reference
- Pointers to context files

**Additional .md files** = Context files - SOPs for specific aspects (loaded on-demand)
- These are Standard Operating Procedures, not just documentation
- They provide specific handling instructions
- Can reference Workflows/, Tools/, etc.

### 🚨 CRITICAL: NO Context/ Subdirectory 🚨

**NEVER create Context/ or Docs/ subdirectories.**

Additional .md files ARE the context files. They live **directly in skill root**.

**WRONG:**
```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md
└── Context/              ❌ NEVER CREATE THIS
    └── Aesthetic.md
```

**CORRECT:**
```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md
├── Aesthetic.md          ✅ Context file in skill root
├── Examples.md           ✅ Context file in skill root
└── Tools.md              ✅ Context file in skill root
```

**The skill directory IS the context.**

### Example Structure

```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md              # 40 lines - minimal routing
├── Aesthetic.md          # Context file - SOP for aesthetic
├── Examples.md           # Context file - SOP for examples
├── Tools.md              # Context file - SOP for tools
├── Workflows/            # Workflows
│   └── Essay.md
└── Tools/                # CLI tools
    └── Generate.ts
```

### Minimal SKILL.md Template

```markdown
---
name: SkillName
description: Create, test, and optimize LifeOS skills — scaffolding, effectiveness testing, description optimization. USE WHEN create skill, new skill, validate skill, test skill, improve skill, optimize description.
---

# SkillName

Brief description.

## Workflow Routing

| Trigger | Workflow |
|---------|----------|
| "trigger" | `Workflows/WorkflowName.md` |

## Quick Reference

**Key points** (3-5 bullet points)

**Full Documentation:**
- Detail 1: `SkillSearch('skillname detail1')` → loads Detail1.md
- Detail 2: `SkillSearch('skillname detail2')` → loads Detail2.md
```

### When To Use

✅ **Use dynamic loading for:**
- SKILL.md > 100 lines
- Multiple documentation sections
- Extensive API reference
- Detailed examples

❌ **Don't use for:**
- Simple skills (< 50 lines)
- Pure utility wrappers (use LIFEOS/TOOLS.md instead)

### Benefits

- **Token Savings:** 70%+ reduction on skill invocation (when full docs not needed)
- **Organization:** SKILL.md = routing, context files = SOPs for specific aspects
- **Efficiency:** Workflows load only what they actually need
- **Maintainability:** Easier to update individual sections

**See:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md` (Dynamic Loading Pattern section)

---


## Workflow Routing

### Structure Workflows (scaffolding and conventions)

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **CreateSkill** | "create a new skill" | `Workflows/CreateSkill.md` |
| **ValidateSkill** | "validate skill", "check skill" | `Workflows/ValidateSkill.md` |
| **UpdateSkill** | "update skill", "add workflow" | `Workflows/UpdateSkill.md` |
| **CanonicalizeSkill** | "canonicalize", "fix skill structure" | `Workflows/CanonicalizeSkill.md` |

### Effectiveness Workflows (testing and optimization)

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **TestSkill** | "test skill", "does this skill work", "skill not working" | `Workflows/TestSkill.md` |
| **ImproveSkill** | "improve skill", "skill quality", "fix skill instructions" | `Workflows/ImproveSkill.md` |
| **OptimizeDescription** | "optimize description", "skill not triggering", "trigger accuracy" | `Workflows/OptimizeDescription.md` |

## Skill Types (Choose Before Building)

Before creating any skill, identify which of the 9 types it is (from Anthropic's internal skill taxonomy, Thariq Shihipar, Mar 2026). The type shapes structure and testing decisions.

| Type | Focus | Key Structure | Example |
|------|-------|---------------|---------|
| 1. Library/API Reference | Gotchas, edge cases Claude gets wrong | Lightweight, gotchas-heavy, reference snippets | HonoReference, D1Reference |
| 2. Product Validation | Test/verify code works | State assertions, browser automation, output recording | Browser |
| 3. Data Fetching | Connect to data systems | Credential refs, query patterns, dashboard pointers | USMetrics, _METRICS |
| 4. Business Process | Automate repetitive workflows | Execution logs, consistency tracking | _CLICKUP, _BROADCAST |
| 5. Code Scaffolding | Generate framework boilerplate | Template files, project-aware scripts | CreateCLI, CreateSkill |
| 6. Code Quality | Enforce standards, review | Deterministic scripts, hook integration | /simplify, /code-review |
| 7. CI/CD & Deployment | Deploy with safety patterns | Pre-deploy checks, smoke tests, rollback | (gap — needs Deploy skill) |
| 8. Operations Runbooks | Map phenomena to diagnostics | Phenomenon → tool → query → report | _HEALTHCHECK |
| 9. Infrastructure Ops | Maintenance with safety guardrails | Safety gates, audit logging, orphan detection | _LIFEOS, _DOTFILES |

## Skill Writing Guidance

When writing or improving skill instructions, follow these principles from Anthropic's skill-creator methodology and Thariq Shihipar's "Lessons from Building Claude Code" (Mar 2026):

### Core Principles

- **Don't state the obvious.** Claude is competent at programming and knows codebases. Focus on information that **breaks Claude's default patterns** — things it gets wrong without guidance. Test: "Would Claude do this wrong without being told?" If not, remove it.
- **Explain the why, not just the what.** Models with good theory of mind + clear reasoning outperform models with rigid constraints. Instead of "ALWAYS use 3 bullets", explain why bullets matter for the audience.
- **Keep it lean.** The context window is a public good. Remove instructions that don't improve output. If test transcripts show the agent wasting time on unproductive steps, cut them. SKILL.md should be under 500 lines.
- **Cut intensifier-only lines.** Stating a rule once is the instruction. `MANDATORY`, `CRITICAL`, "not optional", and a third restatement add volume, not constraint — the model obeys specificity and code, not emphasis. Delete any line whose only content is shouting a rule stated elsewhere. Watch `## Best Practices` / `## Tips` sections: they collect default-restating filler ("be thorough", "keep it simple", "validate carefully"). Run the delete-test in `Prompting/Standards.md` § Signal-to-Noise on every line: cut it, and restore only if you can name the specific non-default behavior it forces.
- **Generalize, don't overfit.** Fix underlying patterns, not specific test failures. The skill will be used on many prompts beyond your test set.
- **Bundle repeated work.** If test agents all independently wrote similar helper scripts, add that script to Tools/ so every future invocation benefits.
- **Set appropriate degrees of freedom.** Match specificity to task fragility. Database migrations need exact commands; code reviews need general direction.
- **Don't over-constrain.** Skills are reused heavily. Avoid overly specific instructions. Provide needed information but leave flexibility for different contexts.

### Description Best Practices

- **Descriptions are for models, not humans.** The description is injected into the system prompt. Claude reads it to decide whether to invoke the skill.
- **Descriptions should be slightly pushy.** Models tend to undertrigger. Name specific scenarios even if the user might not explicitly mention the skill.
- **Include negative triggers for confusable skills.** Add "NOT FOR" clauses when skills share vocabulary: `"NOT FOR web pentesting (use WebAssessment)"`.
- **Undertriggering signals:** Skill doesn't load when it should, users manually invoking it.
- **Overtriggering signals:** Skill loads for irrelevant queries, users disabling it.

### Gotchas Section (MANDATORY)

Every skill MUST have a `## Gotchas` section after the workflow routing table. Thariq: "The highest information density in any Skill comes from gotchas sections."

Populate with:
- API quirks Claude doesn't know about
- Common mistakes observed during usage
- Ordering/sequencing requirements that aren't obvious
- Edge cases that cause silent failures

**Gotchas accumulate over time.** After every skill failure, add the lesson.

### BPE (Bitter-Pilled Engineering) Check

Before finalizing any skill, ask: **"Would a smarter model make this skill unnecessary?"**

- **Anti-fragile (keep):** Verification harnesses, data pipelines, tool wrappers, accumulated gotchas, deterministic scripts
- **Fragile (question):** CoT orchestrators, format parsers, retry cascades, elaborate reasoning scaffolding

Focus skills on knowledge Claude can't derive (failure modes, API quirks), tools Claude can't replicate (API calls, automation), and workflows that benefit from consistency.

### Progressive Disclosure (from Anthropic)

Three levels of information loading — use this to manage large skills:
1. **Level 1 (YAML frontmatter):** Always in system prompt. Triggering info only.
2. **Level 2 (SKILL.md body):** Loaded when skill is invoked. Routing + key guidance.
3. **Level 3 (Reference files):** Root-level `.md` files or `References/` subdirectory loaded on demand.

Tell Claude what files exist; it will read them when appropriate. SKILL.md should be under 500 lines — if over, extract detailed content to reference files.

### Testing Best Practices (from Anthropic)

Three testing levels for skills:
1. **Manual testing** — Run queries and observe behavior
2. **Scripted testing** — Automate test cases (use TestSkill workflow)
3. **Programmatic testing** — Build evaluation suites (use Evals skill)

**Evaluation-driven development:** Define what "this skill working" looks like before building the skill. Iterate on a single challenging task until Claude succeeds, then extract the winning approach.

### On-Demand Hook Pattern (from Anthropic)

Skills can include hooks that activate only when invoked, remaining effective for the session:
- `/careful` — Intercept dangerous commands (rm -rf, DROP TABLE, force-push)
- `/freeze` — Block edits outside specific directories
- `/audit` — Log all tool calls for session review

*All guidance above derived from Thariq Shihipar's "Lessons from Building Claude Code" (Mar 2026), Anthropic's official skill guide, and platform documentation.*

## Examples

# Interview Me

End-of-workday synthesis ritual. The user is a sport-science / performance analyst who writes essays connecting sport science, product strategy, and decision-making. The interview's job is to extract publishable insights, not to record what happened.

## Vault location

`/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain/`

**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.

- `Inbox/` — full transcripts (one per day)
- `Notes/` — atomic permanent notes (one idea per file)
- `Drafts/` — essays in progress
- `Archive/` — published
- `Templates/interview-note.md`, `Templates/permanent-note.md`

## The interview

**Time budget:** 10–15 minutes. If the user wants to keep talking, schedule a follow-up session — don't blow the budget.

**Opening line (verbatim is fine):**
> Let's debrief. Four short questions, then I write up anything that earned its place. Ready?

### Question 1 — Orientation (filter)
> What did you spend time on today?

Listen for themes. Don't try to capture everything. Look for: a hard decision, a piece of work that consumed a lot of time, anything that felt different from yesterday.

### Question 2 — Signal (insight detection)
> What surprised you, frustrated you, or changed your mind?

This is the gold question. Genuine surprise, frustration, or updated belief = the moments worth writing down. If the answer is "nothing," probe once: *"Nothing at all? Even small recalibrations count."* If still nothing, accept and move on — not every day produces signal.

### Question 3 — Pattern (synthesis)
> Does anything from today connect to what you were thinking about earlier this week or recently?

**Optional aid:** quietly Glob `Notes/*.md` modified in the last 7 days; if you find 2–3 candidates that match today's themes, name them and ask if today's experience updates them.

### Question 4 — Essay seed (publishable insight)
> If you told a peer one thing about today's work, what would it be?

This question converts experience into transferable insight. If the user gives a great one-liner — capture it verbatim as the seed for a permanent note.

## Optional source pull-ins

Offer when the user references them. Don't pull unprompted.

- **Meeting referenced** ("today's call with X", "this morning's standup"):
  → **First, check `Inbox/meetings/` for a local summary** — Glob for files matching the date or participant. If found, read and quote from the local file (free, fast, no API call).
  → If not found locally, ask: *"Want me to pull from Fireflies?"* → invoke the `meeting-sync` skill to sync the latest meetings, then read the local file.
  → Fall back to direct `pp-fireflies` only if `meeting-sync` reports nothing matching.
- **Paper / article referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the source from Zotero?" → use `pp-zotero-research-library` skill.
- **GPS / Catapult data referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the underlying metric?" → use `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` skill.

Quote sources in the note's frontmatter `source:` field or the **Evidence / origin** section.

## Output protocol

### Always write the transcript

`Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-interview.md` — full Q&A, lightly cleaned. Use the `Templates/interview-note.md` skeleton. Fill in `themes`, `notes_produced`, `pulled_sources` in frontmatter.

### Write 0–3 permanent notes

**Bias toward fewer notes.** A vault full of mediocre notes is worse than one with three great ones. If nothing crossed the bar today, write zero — say so to the user. They will respect this.

A note earns its place if it meets at least one of:
- States a transferable claim (works beyond today's context)
- Updates a previously held view (in which case, also update / link the old note)
- Names a pattern across two or more recent days
- Is a clean essay seed the user could draft from later

Each note goes to `Notes/<concept-title-kebab-case>.md` with the `Templates/permanent-note.md` skeleton filled in:
- `created`: today's date
- `source`: `[[YYYY-MM-DD-interview]]`
- `domain`: pick from `sport-science`, `product`, `decision-making`, `leadership`, `methodology`, `personal`
- `tags`: free-form, but reuse existing tags from other Notes when possible
- Body: claim in 1–2 sentences, why it matters, evidence/origin, connections (use `[[wikilink]]` to related Notes), open questions

### Memory bridge (when warranted)

If the interview surfaces a **durable** fact about the user, their projects, or working style that should persist across Claude sessions:
- Also write a Tier A memory file via the `memory-write` skill (it derives the correct project slug from the current working directory) or update USER.md / project_*.md as appropriate.
- Tell the user explicitly: "Also saved this to memory as <name>."
- Do NOT bridge ephemeral notes. Most permanent notes stay in the vault only.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't pad notes with model commentary.** The user's own words and insights are the value. You are a scribe with editorial judgment, not a co-author.
- **Don't ask follow-up questions beyond the four** unless an answer was genuinely ambiguous and one clarification unlocks a much better note.
- **Don't produce a note "just to have one."** Zero notes is an honest output.
- **Don't break the 10–15 min budget.** Offer a follow-up session if needed.
- **Don't write to `Drafts/` from a daily interview.** Drafts come out of weekly synthesis, not daily capture.

## Weekly synthesis

Weekly synthesis is NOT this skill's job. If the user says "weekly synthesis", "weekly review", or asks to look across the week, invoke the `weekly-review` skill — it owns the Friday ritual (themes, project status, decisions, stale action items, essay angles). This skill is strictly the daily debrief.

## End-of-session sign-off

Always end with a brief summary:
- Transcript saved: `Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-interview.md`
- Notes created: list with paths and one-line summaries
- Memory bridge: yes/no, what
- Any open thread to revisit tomorrow

Keep it tight — three to five lines.

**Three questions, asked before the reflection questions.** Facts are easier to recall
than insight when the user is tired, and a hard 90-second opener is what makes the ritual
survivable nightly. Reflection quality does not suffer from coming second; it suffers
from the user never starting.

This part exists because `status-report` — the biweekly email to the user's supervisors —
has a sourcing gap: roughly two thirds of what belongs in that email (equipment arriving,
installs, who onboarded onto what, hallway conversations, follow-ups awaiting a reply)
appears in **no** automated source. Without a nightly log, the report has to reconstruct
two weeks from memory. With one, it mostly writes itself.

Ask all three at once. Accept short answers. Do not probe.

> Quick log first, 90 seconds. Then the usual four.
> 1. Anything arrive, get installed, or change hands today? Who's onboarding onto it?
> 2. Who did you talk to that Kenny or Chris would want to know about? Names and sport.
> 3. Waiting on anyone, or anything about to go sideways?

**Honest zero rule.** If all three are genuinely "nothing", write **no file**. A day with
no operational facts is a real day. Padding this log is worse than skipping it, because
`status-report` trusts these entries verbatim.

### Output — `{vault_status_log}/YYYY-MM-DD.md`

```markdown
---
date: YYYY-MM-DD
sports: [Football, Tennis]      # programs named in the answers; [] if none
---

## Equipment & installs
- Perch cameras installed at Foster. Football onboarding this week.

## People & conversations
- Javi (Tennis) — FirstBeat onboarding, wants a one-pager for his staff.

## Waiting on / risks
- Micah, no reply since 8/17.
```

Use the user's own words. Do not editorialize, rank, or add commentary — `status-report`
does the judgement pass later, and it needs raw facts to judge.

**Append, never overwrite.** If today's file exists (a second debrief, or a correction),

- `Drafts/` — essays in progress
- `Archive/` — published
- `Templates/interview-note.md`, `Templates/permanent-note.md`
- `Inbox/status-log/` — daily supervisor fact logs (Part 0). Path key: `vault_status_log`.

---

## Part 0 — Supervisor log (90 seconds, ask first)

**Three questions, asked before the reflection questions.** Facts are easier to recall
than insight when the user is tired, and a hard 90-second opener is what makes the ritual
survivable nightly. Reflection quality does not suffer from coming second; it suffers
from the user never starting.

This part exists because `status-report` — the biweekly email to the user's supervisors —
has a sourcing gap: roughly two thirds of what belongs in that email (equipment arriving,
installs, who onboarded onto what, hallway conversations, follow-ups awaiting a reply)
appears in **no** automated source. Without a nightly log, the report has to reconstruct
two weeks from memory. With one, it mostly writes itself.

Ask all three at once. Accept short answers. Do not probe.

> Quick log first, 90 seconds. Then the usual four.
> 1. Anything arrive, get installed, or change hands today? Who's onboarding onto it?
> 2. Who did you talk to that Kenny or Chris would want to know about? Names and sport.
> 3. Waiting on anyone, or anything about to go sideways?

**Honest zero rule.** If all three are genuinely "nothing", write **no file**. A day with
no operational facts is a real day. Padding this log is worse than skipping it, because
`status-report` trusts these entries verbatim.

### Output — `{vault_status_log}/YYYY-MM-DD.md`

```markdown
---
date: YYYY-MM-DD
sports: [Football, Tennis]      # programs named in the answers; [] if none
---

## Equipment & installs
- Perch cameras installed at Foster. Football onboarding this week.

## People & conversations
- Javi (Tennis) — FirstBeat onboarding, wants a one-pager for his staff.

## Waiting on / risks
- Micah, no reply since 8/17.
```

Use the user's own words. Do not editorialize, rank, or add commentary — `status-report`
does the judgement pass later, and it needs raw facts to judge.

**Append, never overwrite.** If today's file exists (a second debrief, or a correction),
add to the existing sections rather than replacing the file.

**This log never becomes a permanent note.** It is a fact record for one downstream
consumer. Insight goes in `Notes/` via Part 1, which is why the skill's "NOT a journaling
app" rule still holds.

---

## Part 1 — The interview

**Time budget:** 10–15 minutes total including Part 0. If the user wants to keep talking, schedule a follow-up session — don't blow the budget.

**Opening line (verbatim is fine):**
> Now the four. Then I write up anything that earned its place.

### Question 1 — Orientation (filter)
> What did you spend time on today?

Listen for themes. Don't try to capture everything. Look for: a hard decision, a piece of work that consumed a lot of time, anything that felt different from yesterday.

### Question 2 — Signal (insight detection)
> What surprised you, frustrated you, or changed your mind?

This is the gold question. Genuine surprise, frustration, or updated belief = the moments worth writing down. If the answer is "nothing," probe once: *"Nothing at all? Even small recalibrations count."* If still nothing, accept and move on — not every day produces signal.

### Question 3 — Pattern (synthesis)
> Does anything from today connect to what you were thinking about earlier this week or recently?

**Optional aid:** quietly Glob `Notes/*.md` modified in the last 7 days; if you find 2–3 candidates that match today's themes, name them and ask if today's experience updates them.

### Question 4 — Essay seed (publishable insight)
> If you told a peer one thing about today's work, what would it be?

This question converts experience into transferable insight. If the user gives a great one-liner — capture it verbatim as the seed for a permanent note.

## Optional source pull-ins

Offer when the user references them. Don't pull unprompted.

- **Meeting referenced** ("today's call with X", "this morning's standup"):
  → **First, check `Inbox/meetings/` for a local summary** — Glob for files matching the date or participant. If found, read and quote from the local file (free, fast, no API call).
  → If not found locally, ask: *"Want me to pull from Fireflies?"* → invoke the `meeting-sync` skill to sync the latest meetings, then read the local file.
  → Fall back to direct `pp-fireflies` only if `meeting-sync` reports nothing matching.
- **Paper / article referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the source from Zotero?" → use `pp-zotero-research-library` skill.
- **GPS / Catapult data referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the underlying metric?" → use `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` skill.

Quote sources in the note's frontmatter `source:` field or the **Evidence / origin** section.

## Output protocol

### Write the supervisor log (unless all three answers were nothing)

`Inbox/status-log/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — see Part 0 for the shape. Write this **first**, before
the transcript, so a session that gets cut short still leaves the report its facts.

### Always write the transcript

`Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-interview.md` — full Q&A, lightly cleaned. Use the `Templates/interview-note.md` skeleton. Fill in `themes`, `notes_produced`, `pulled_sources` in frontmatter.

### Write 0–3 permanent notes

**Bias toward fewer notes.** A vault full of mediocre notes is worse than one with three great ones. If nothing crossed the bar today, write zero — say so to the user. They will respect this.

A note earns its place if it meets at least one of:
- States a transferable claim (works beyond today's context)
- Updates a previously held view (in which case, also update / link the old note)
- Names a pattern across two or more recent days
- Is a clean essay seed the user could draft from later

Each note goes to `Notes/<concept-title-kebab-case>.md` with the `Templates/permanent-note.md` skeleton filled in:
- `created`: today's date
- `source`: `[[YYYY-MM-DD-interview]]`
- `domain`: pick from `sport-science`, `product`, `decision-making`, `leadership`, `methodology`, `personal`
- `tags`: free-form, but reuse existing tags from other Notes when possible
- Body: claim in 1–2 sentences, why it matters, evidence/origin, connections (use `[[wikilink]]` to related Notes), open questions

### Memory bridge (when warranted)

If the interview surfaces a **durable** fact about the user, their projects, or working style that should persist across Claude sessions:
- Also write a Tier A memory file via the `memory-write` skill (it derives the correct project slug from the current working directory) or update USER.md / project_*.md as appropriate.
- Tell the user explicitly: "Also saved this to memory as <name>."
- Do NOT bridge ephemeral notes. Most permanent notes stay in the vault only.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't pad notes with model commentary.** The user's own words and insights are the value. You are a scribe with editorial judgment, not a co-author.
- **Don't ask follow-up questions beyond the four** unless an answer was genuinely ambiguous and one clarification unlocks a much better note.
- **Don't produce a note "just to have one."** Zero notes is an honest output.
- **Don't break the 10–15 min budget.** Offer a follow-up session if needed.
- **Don't write to `Drafts/` from a daily interview.** Drafts come out of weekly synthesis, not daily capture.

## Weekly synthesis

Weekly synthesis is NOT this skill's job. If the user says "weekly synthesis", "weekly review", or asks to look across the week, invoke the `weekly-review` skill — it owns the Friday ritual (themes, project status, decisions, stale action items, essay angles). This skill is strictly the daily debrief.

## End-of-session sign-off

Always end with a brief summary:
- Transcript saved: `Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-interview.md`
- Notes created: list with paths and one-line summaries
- Memory bridge: yes/no, what
- Any open thread to revisit tomorrow

Keep it tight — three to five lines.

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence (commit+push to KeystoneOS is standing-authorized per `feedback-auto-commit-push`; for any OTHER repo with changes, commit locally and list the push as an open item instead of pushing).

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` in every repo touched this session (check cwd first, then any repo mentioned in the conversation; if session context is thin, check `KeystoneOS` and any `DEV/` repo with commits dated today).
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- KeystoneOS: stage, commit with a descriptive message, push. Authorized.
- Other repos with changes: commit locally with a descriptive message; do NOT push without asking — list it in the final report instead.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Never push to a repo other than KeystoneOS without explicit approval.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# Shell / Environment (macOS)

- zsh/bash is the native surface on this machine. PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`) is installed only to run the KeystoneOS `.ps1` jobs natively.
- **The tool-path list has one home: `~/.claude/TOOLPATHS.md`.** Read that file when you need a path. It is deliberately not inlined here — this file loads into every session in every project, and the table answers a question asked on only a few of them. Only the traps below are kept, because acting on them wrongly is expensive.
- **Verify, don't trust any list.** Tools have existed in two places before, with the older one
  winning. `which -a <tool>` is authoritative. To read PATH honestly, scrub the environment first —
  a PATH read from inside a tool shell is polluted by that shell's own exports:
  `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" TERM=xterm SHELL=/bin/zsh /bin/zsh -lic 'echo $PATH'`
- Traps:
  - Python is PEP 668-managed — use venvs or `uv`, never `pip install` globally.
  - `uv` is a standalone install at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv`, **not** Homebrew. Claude Code hooks call that absolute path; do not delete or relocate it.
  - `timeout` is NOT installed (no GNU coreutils). Don't use it in scripts.
  - Homebrew owns `/opt/homebrew/bin`. `/usr/local/bin` is empty and stays that way — never install into it.
  - Secrets live in the macOS Keychain, not in `~/.zshrc`.
- DEV projects live at `~/DEV` (not `~/Desktop/DEV`).

# Workflow Expectations

- When asked to **create, merge, or consolidate an artifact** (calendar, deck, doc), the expected deliverable is always a produced file. Verify what exists first, then create the artifact regardless — never conclude with "it already exists" instead of delivering the file.
- When the user types `/graphify`, invoke the Skill tool with `skill: "graphify"` before doing anything else.

# Session Startup

Handled by the `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook — do not read these files by hand. It injects `global-memory/USER.md`, `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, `transcripts/.errors.log` (only when non-empty), and a pointer to the KeystoneOS snapshot.

- If `.errors.log` content appears, surface it once on the first response, then continue. It is normally empty; entries mean hook failures.
- If a **"SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file"** block appears, say so on the first response instead of working around it.
- **If no `## User profile` block is in context at session start, the hook did not fire.** Say so, then read `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` and `transcripts/.errors.log` by hand.
- What the hook injects is a frozen snapshot. Mid-session writes take effect next session. Never load more than this proactively.

# Memory — routing only

The two-tier memory system (`~/.claude/global-memory/` and `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`) is owned by the **`memory-write` skill**, which holds the tier rules, character caps, slug rules, write steps, retrieval ladder, and daily-compiled-log rules.

The active project's Tier A memory (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`, indexed by its `MEMORY.md`) is **auto-injected by the harness** each session. Tier A files are also indexed by memsearch, so they stay recallable across projects.

- Writing a fact — "remember this", "note that", "save this", "forget about" → `Skill("memory-write")`
- Recalling past context — "did we already…?", "what did we decide about X" → `Skill("memory-write")`, retrieval-ladder section
- Daily compiled logs at `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/` are owned by `claude-memory-compiler`. Never hand-edit them; never read them eagerly.
- **Never write to a `C--Users-eric-rash*` slug** — pre-migration Windows keys, retired 2026-08-14. Still recallable via memsearch, never auto-injected again.

Do not restate the memory procedure in this file. It has one home, and that home is the skill.

---

`AGENTS.md` is the sibling of this file for harnesses that have no Skill tool (Codex and similar). It intentionally carries the memory rules as plain prose instead of routing to a skill. **The two files are not meant to be identical — do not "fix" the difference by symlinking them.**

# ~/DEV — workspace map

Eric Rash — Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics. Sport science and
football analytics, plus the agent system that runs them.

This file is a **map, not a rulebook**. Behavior rules live in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read only the index you need.

| Football | `FOOTBALL.md` | Game film, player analytics, CFB prediction. ~39k files — about two thirds of DEV. |

## Elsewhere on disk

|---|---|

## Layout rules

Full rules — grouping depth, the depth-2 discovery limit, and the gitignored-subtree
trap — live in project memory: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

turn**. A stale pointer is worse than no pointer.

The counts above are approximate on purpose — they convey scale, not state, and
a `~` keeps ordinary growth from making this file wrong. Re-measure them only
when one is off by enough to change a decision. Counts last checked 2026-09-05.
